status: Wrist ADC/driver candidate; switched-capacitor approximation and hardware verification required

buffer.model_note: The current official OPA320 product page links a Q1 model. This study selects the matching Q1 part rather than treating its model as a verified catalog-part model.
buffer.feedback: Local unity feedback from amplifier output pin; ADC filter is outside the loop

adc.interface: 3-wire CS mode; DIN tied to DVDD, CONVST is conversion/CS, rising-edge SPI reads
adc.limits: Reference, sampling switch behavior, capacitor reset state and quantizer are not a complete manufacturer ADC model. ADC INL/noise/offset and system accuracy require measurement.

filter.negative_connection: AINN connects through its series resistor to local ADC ground, not the 1.65 V tactile bias
filter.source_note: ADS8866 figure 51 shows balanced series resistors and a differential capacitor. The text gives both a 20-times rule and >590 pF; 2.2 nF exceeds both interpretations of the 59 pF input capacitance.
filter.revision_note: The first simulation with only the differential capacitor produced negative-input excursions outside the declared absolute-input range in two completed cases. Add 2.2 nF from each ADC input to local ADC ground to absorb common-mode charge steps. Preserve the earlier failed/incomplete run.

reference.connection: OUT_F and OUT_S meet at the ADC REF land; GND_S returns separately to the ADC ground land. The 47 milliohm resistor is in series with the output capacitor, not the ADC reference feed.
reference.note: Verify capacitance after voltage/temperature derating and include capacitor/trace ESR. The datasheet requires 10-47 uF with a capacitance-dependent ESR stability region. This is a selected implementation target, not a verified reference circuit.

screen.integration_note: Second-order Gear is a separate numerical follow-up to saved trapezoidal runs that aborted. It can add numerical damping, so retain independent AC results and compare completed trapezoidal traces plus a smaller time-step replay before interpreting transient settling.
limits: The sample switch uses the declared resistance values, not a TI guarantee of the internal switch resistance.
Resetting the capacitors to both rails probes charge steps; it is an explicit stimulus assumption, not a claim about the ADC's internal reset sequence.
Only the ADC sampling capacitance is doubled. External filter capacitors retain nominal values. This is a sensitivity study, not a probabilistic manufacturing bound.
The reference source is ideal in this driver-only simulation. REF6033 stability, supply coupling, layout and ADC digital timing are separate checks.
No force, contact probability or effective ADC resolution is inferred.
